title: Putting the Path in Time: Jerk Limited Profiles That Respect Every Joint, the Stop at Every Corner, and the Cost of a Path With Many Vertices

questions.question: What does the jerk limit of an S curve prevent?
options: A step in the acceleration, which shakes the arm and its gearboxes
The speed passing its limit
The arm stopping at a vertex
A move taking longer than it need
questions.explanation: The acceleration ramps up and down and never jumps. A jump in acceleration is a jump in torque, which the gears and the links feel as a knock.

questions.question: The S curve and the trapezoid for a move of 1 rad took:
options: 1.000 s both
questions.explanation: Ramping the acceleration costs about the ramp's time. The trapezoid is quicker because it is allowed what the arm cannot do well.

questions.question: The trapezoid's jerk over a millisecond step was:
options: 20 rad/s3, the limit
4 rad/s3
4000 rad/s3
Zero: a trapezoid has no jerk
questions.explanation: Its acceleration goes from nothing to 4 rad/s2 in one step. Over a millisecond that is 4000 rad/s3, two hundred times the limit.

questions.question: The wandering path of 17 points took 14.33 s and its straight shortcut:
options: 14.33 s, the same: the limits are the same
7.2 s, about half
questions.explanation: Every vertex is a stop and a start. Seventeen points are sixteen moves from rest to rest, where the shortcut was one.

questions.question: How are a joint's limits turned into limits along a segment?
options: The limit of the joint that moves the most, alone
The smallest, over the joints, of the joint's limit over its share of the direction
The average of the joints' limits
The largest, over the joints, of limit over share
questions.explanation: Each joint takes a share of the motion along the segment. The speed along it may rise until the first joint reaches its own limit.

questions.question: Why did halving the speed limits not change a short move?
options: The override applies only to long moves
A short move never reaches its cruise speed: acceleration and jerk limit it
A short move is limited by the jerk alone
It did change, by less than the rounding
questions.explanation: A short move spends all its time speeding up and slowing down. Halving a cruise speed it never reaches changes nothing; the long move went from 3.70 to 6.45 s.
